author: j. r. johnson
title: Rep. Gabe Vasquez addresses El Paso airspace closure and border security concerns
text:
Rep. Gabe Vasquez, who represents New Mexico’s 2nd district in the U.S. Congress, has used his social media platform to address recent concerns ranging from airspace closures to border security and allegations of sexual abuse involving a public figure.
On March 17, 2026, Vasquez referenced ongoing efforts to obtain information regarding an unexpected closure of El Paso airspace. He wrote, “It’s been over a month since @RepEscobar and I demanded answers on the chaotic, surprise closure of the El Paso airspace. New Mexicans deserve answers, and I plan to get them.”
Later that day, Vasquez commented on border security strategies in the region. In his post dated March 17, 2026, he stated: “Five Texas Sheriffs are echoing what I’ve been saying — we should be strengthening border security with smart technology, not physical barriers, in places like Big Bend National Park and the Continental Divide in New Mexico’s Bootheel. Taxpayer dollars should be spent wisely for”
On March 18, 2026, Vasquez addressed another issue by posting: “My statement on sexual abuse allegations against Cesar Chavez”
Vasquez has served as the representative for New Mexico’s 2nd District since 2023 after defeating Yvette Herrell in the general election held in 2024 with a narrow margin of victory—winning 52.1% of the vote to Herrell’s 47.9%. Born in El Paso, Texas in 1984 and currently residing in Las Cruces at age 38, Vasquez is an alumnus of New Mexico State University where he earned his BA degree in 2008.
